data.title: bn-18w74: signing custody across restart — LocalKeystore persistence, keystore-backed launcher, own/adopted separation

data.body:
[high] Model the post-rename directory-sync failure as an uncertain or committed result.

At line 1326, rename has already replaced signing-state. A failure from sync_dir at line 1327 therefore returns Err after the new state is visible and may be durable. The daemon maps every custody Err to an in-memory rollback and PublicationAborted at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:764-771. A restart can then load the new rotation, revocation, mint, or adoption even though the caller received an abort that says nothing changed. This violates the typed-inconclusiveness and atomic-result contract.

Failure modes: directory fsync can fail after a successful rename, including I/O failure or filesystems with unsupported directory sync.
Edge cases: key-making changes already have the successor key file; adoption and revocation can silently appear only after restart.
Rollback: the current in-memory rollback does not roll back the renamed state. Either retain the new in-memory state after the commit point, or expose an explicit outcome-unknown state and reconcile from custody. A second rename is itself fallible and ambiguous.
Monitoring: preserve and count the post-commit ambiguity. The current Erased custody converts it to unit and loses the commit phase.
Validation: add a deterministic fault seam after rename and at directory sync. For mint, rotate, revoke, and adoption, assert that the wire result, live authority, and relaunched authority agree. No PublicationAborted result may later become an applied state.

[medium] Reject a restored own-key compromise revocation when its relay link is missing.

The completeness check at lines 270-279 covers only SignerStanding::Rotated. A normal compromised revocation moves the own key pre-signature into own_links at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:1873-1881. If a decoded custody state keeps the audit record but omits that revocation link, validate_custody currently accepts it. After restart, export_links cannot relay the revocation, so another registry can continue to accept signatures from the compromised key.

Require every own key whose standing is Revoked { reason: Compromised, .. } to have its verified LinkEvent::Revoked entry in own_links. Add a restart test that removes only that link from a valid post-revocation state and expects CustodyRefusal.

data.reason: BLOCK: [high] post-rename sync failures can return PublicationAborted while the new signing state is loaded after restart; [medium] restore validation accepts an own compromised revocation with its relay link removed.

data.body: [high] The repair still reports success when durability is unknown. crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:823-830 keeps the new state and returns Ok after CustodyWrite::Unconfirmed. crates/continuum-security/src/keystore.rs:1423 classifies a failed directory sync that way. A visible rename is not proven crash-durable until the parent directory sync succeeds. The test at crates/continuumd/tests/signing_custody.rs:1277-1281 only drops and reopens the live filesystem. It does not model loss of the unsynced rename. Failure modes: a sync error, power loss, kernel crash, or storage reset can restore the old directory entry after the wire reported success. Edge cases: a successful compromise revocation can disappear, a retired key can become active again, or a mint, rotation, loss recovery, or adopted revocation can vanish after restart. Rollback: do not claim rollback after rename. Return an explicit outcome-unknown result, or quarantine signing and reconcile against a durability-confirmed state before any success claim. The absent IDL shape does not make success sound. Monitoring: custody_unconfirmed and unconfirmed_writes are memory-only and disappear on restart. Persist or externally expose the ambiguity and prevent normal signing while it remains. Validation: add a crash-consistency oracle that can choose either old or new durable directory entry after failed sync. Assert that no success response can later reload the old state, especially for compromise revocation.

[medium] Fixed at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:289-298. Restored compromised own keys now require their recorded, verified revocation link. The regression at crates/continuumd/tests/signing_custody.rs:1302-1347 removes that link and expects CustodyRefusal::OwnLink.

data.reason: The target validates the compromised own-key revocation link and includes a restart regression.

[high] Post-rename directory-sync failure returns success although the rename is not crash-durable. A restart after power loss can restore a revoked key or lose a completed rotation, mint, recovery, or adoption.

data.body: [resolved] d0407fcd writes and syncs a pending marker before rename, returns non-retryable OutcomeUnknown after an unconfirmed commit, quarantines every signing path, and validates then sweeps whichever state survives at relaunch. The crash oracle covers old and new durable entries for mint, rotate, revoke, and adoption. Protocol 3.9 gating prevents this code from reaching older clients. Static inspection confirms the prior wrong-success and wrong-abort paths are closed.

data.reason: Fixed at d0407fcd: typed OutcomeUnknown, durable pending marker, quarantine, and old-or-new crash reconciliation.

data.body:
[medium] Correct the semantic review record before it becomes gate evidence.

At tools/governance/reviews/bn-18w74.toml:43-49, the record says there are no wire changes and that the protocol and IDL are unchanged. This target changes IDL 1.16 to 1.17, protocol 3.8 to 3.9, adds ErrorCode::OutcomeUnknown, adds it to four operation error clauses, and adds rule signing.custody. The migration note also predates that repair. A machine-readable review record that denies the actual wire change can mislead the separate human approval and migration review, even though the code gates pre-3.9 clients correctly. Keep updated empty if this field only inventories JSON schemas, but revise the reason, change summary, and migration note to name the additive versioned wire change and its compatibility boundary.

data.body:
[medium] Reject restored peer rotations whose relay link is missing.

`validate_custody` checks only links present in `adopted_links`. It never checks them for completeness against the audit log. The normal adoption path records a peer rotation and retains its link at lines 1316-1323. No local operation can record a rotation between non-own keys.

A decoded state can therefore keep that rotation in the registry while omitting its only relay link. Restart accepts the split state. `export_links` at lines 1028-1042 then cannot relay the transition. A downstream registry can keep the retired key active and accept new signatures from it.

Require each recorded rotation between non-own keys to have its verified adopted link. Add a restart test that removes only the peer rotation link from a valid state and expects `CustodyRefusal::AdoptedLink`.

data.reason: [medium] Restored peer rotations can omit their adopted relay link. Restart accepts the split state, and later exports cannot propagate the retirement.

data.body: [medium] Fixed at crates/continuumd/src/daemon/signing.rs:291-304. The audit-log sweep now requires each peer rotation to have its adopted link. The regression at crates/continuumd/tests/signing_custody.rs:1573 removes that link and expects CustodyRefusal::AdoptedLink.

data.reason: The target now checks every peer rotation record for its adopted link and includes the restart regression.

data.body: Line correction: the peer-rotation removal starts at crates/continuumd/tests/signing_custody.rs:1586 and the expected AdoptedLink refusal is at line 1597.

[medium] Correct the binding ADR protocol claims. Line 260 says this bn-18w74 revision has no wire or protocol change. Line 365 repeats that claim. The same revision adds OutcomeUnknown, IDL 1.17, protocol 3.9, four operation error clauses, and a pre-3.9 refusal gate. See crates/continuumd/src/protocol/registry.rs:22-33 and notes/plan/schemas/continuumd-native-protocol.idl:5101-5119. The RFC and governance record describe the change, but this binding ADR contradicts them.

Failure modes: migration or release review can treat durable custody as 3.8-compatible and miss the required refusal boundary.
Edge cases: a custody-backed daemon refuses four writes below 3.9, while a daemon without custody still serves them at 3.8. The ADR must preserve that split.
Rollback: this is a documentation correction. Do not remove the 3.9 runtime gate unless the IDL, RFC, registry, and error behavior are rolled back together.
Monitoring: add or extend dossier validation so an ADR protocol claim cannot disagree with the normative IDL version and its governance record.
Validation: revise lines 260 and 365 to state the additive 3.9 change. Keep no JSON-schema, signed-encoding, and semantic-epoch change as separate claims. Run the dossier validator and the full check gate.
